newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says Brazil import deal satisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Chile says Brazil import deal satisfactory.

text.p: Chile has accepted as satisfactory an agreement struck with the Brazilian government to limit the impact of financing restrictions on imports to Brazil, said Chile Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia.
"This mechanism resolves the fundamental problems which we had," Garcia told officials at the economy ministry by telephone from Brazil.
Garcia travelled to Brazil on Thursday to discuss the trade dispute with the Brazilian authorities.
Chile is an associate member of the Mercosur trade bloc, which links Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
Garca said the measures adopted by Brazil did not violate Chile's trade agreement with Mercosur and did not imply an increase in tariffs on imports.
"We have confirmed that (the measures) are not preventing the granting of real loans. What is being prevented is using (these loans) for financial speculation," said Garca.
"And so it is not a measure operating as a parallel tariff."
Brasilia agreed Thursday to include Chile in a deal struck with full Mercosur members to mitigate the impact of the measures, which were announced last week.
The pact will be in force for 120 days and Chilean offficials said they hope to use this period to negotiate the complete lifting of the measures.
